content: For individuals diagnosed with type 1 diabetes, certain non-insulin injectable medications, such as pramlintide and GLP-1 receptor agonists, can play a role in supporting glycemic control. Pramlintide, which has been approved specifically for use in type 1 diabetes, provides modest reductions in hemoglobin A1C levels and body weight. However, it is important to note that pramlintide is not a replacement for insulin therapy. On the other hand, GLP-1 receptor agonists are currently only approved for the treatment of type 2 diabetes. Despite this, studies have demonstrated that these agents can offer modest benefits in individuals with type 1 diabetes, including slight improvements in weight management, reductions in insulin dosage requirements, and better control of A1C levels.
